# Data Model & Contracts Completeness Checklist: Application Foundation

**Purpose**: Pre-`/speckit-implement` review of data-model.md and contracts/ completeness against tasks.md and spec.md — closing gaps before code is written.
**Created**: 2026-08-26
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Is the `VersionInfo` type (introduced by tasks.md T022/T024) documented as an entity in data-model.md, alongside `HealthStatus`? [Gap, data-model.md vs tasks.md T022/T024]
- [ ] CHK002 Does a contract file exist for `GET /api/version` (implemented by tasks.md T023), analogous to [contracts/health-api.md](../contracts/health-api.md)? [Gap, contracts/ vs tasks.md T023]
- [ ] CHK003 Is a generic error-response shape (e.g., fields returned by the centralized error-handling middleware from tasks.md T012) documented anywhere, or only described narratively as "a 5xx JSON error response"? [Gap, contracts/health-api.md §Error Behavior]
- [ ] CHK004 Does data-model.md or quickstart.md describe validation for `VersionInfo`, mirroring the validation rules already given for `HealthStatus`? [Gap, data-model.md]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK005 Are the "key attributes" listed for Frontend Application and Backend Service in data-model.md ("transient UI/connection state", "no persisted state") specific enough to be verified, or are they only illustrative placeholders? [Clarity, data-model.md]
- [ ] CHK006 Is the exact set of types the Frontend Application "imports from the Shared Domain Package" enumerated, or left implicit? [Clarity, data-model.md §Frontend Application]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK007 Is the list of backend routes referenced across data-model.md, contracts/, and tasks.md (health, version) consistent — i.e., does every route implemented in tasks.md have a matching contract, and does every documented contract have a corresponding task? [Consistency, contracts/ vs tasks.md]
- [ ] CHK008 Are the `BACKEND_PORT`/`FRONTEND_DEV_PORT` environment variables named identically across data-model.md's Development Environment Configuration entity and tasks.md T011's `.env.example`? [Consistency, data-model.md vs tasks.md T011]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK009 Does quickstart.md's validation checklist include a step exercising `GET /api/version` (User Story 2), or only `GET /api/health`? [Gap, quickstart.md]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK010 Is the exact JSON shape returned for a `405 Method Not Allowed` response (mentioned in contracts/health-api.md) documented, or only its status code? [Gap, contracts/health-api.md §Error Behavior]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK011 Is the data-model.md's disclaimer ("this feature introduces no persisted data") still accurate given that `VersionInfo` (T022/T024) is in-memory/static data returned by an endpoint — does this distinction need clarifying? [Assumption, data-model.md intro]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [ ] CHK012 Does data-model.md's note that `HealthStatus.status` "MAY add `degraded`/`down` in a future revision" conflict with FR-003's "reports whether the backend is running correctly," which could be read as requiring more than a binary literal today? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-003 vs data-model.md]
- [ ] CHK013 Is it unambiguous whether `VersionInfo` is considered part of this feature's core contract surface (and therefore requires the same rigor as `HealthStatus`) or an illustrative/example addition exempt from full documentation? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-011 vs tasks.md T023]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Items CHK001-CHK002 restate findings F1/F2 from the prior `/speckit-analyze` report (still unresolved)
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
